data.description:
Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire

## Summary
Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` so the scene supplies and uses the same clock. The beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatScene._autoFire` uses the shared beat clock; player shots are emitted on beat ticks.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymWeapons._autoFire` uses the same shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat clock is anchored at scene start and advances with game time.
- [ ] **AC4** — If the game pauses, the beat clock pauses with it.
- [ ] **AC5** — No per-scene duplicate beat modules — one shared instance.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives/uses the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives/uses the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — beat clock wired into auto-fire.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — beat clock wired into gym auto-fire.

## Risks
- Low: straightforward wiring. Must ensure the beat clock is instantiated once and shared.
data.title: Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire

Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing

## Summary
Make the default BPM, per-weapon subdivisions (or fire-rate multiples), and quantisation behaviour configurable through the projects existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/constants.ts`). Include sane defaults. Tests must assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — BPM is configurable through the existing rules/config system with a default of 80.
- [ ] **AC2** — Per-weapon subdivisions (or fire rates) are configurable through the same system.
- [ ] **AC3** — Config overrides are tested: changing BPM or a subdivision changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC4** — No scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals — all values come from the config or are derived from it.
- [ ] **AC5** — The config system handles corrupt/missing config gracefully, falling back to defaults.
- [ ] **AC6** — Subdivisions are configured as positive integers and each fire rate is derived from the beat period, so the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant (parent AC3) holds by construction; a test asserts the invariant under a non-default config.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC4** — [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Key Files
- `src/core/rules.ts` or `src/core/constants.ts` — configurable BPM + subdivisions.
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — reads config for BPM.
- Tests for config override → cadence change.

## Risks
- Medium: choosing the right config home (rules.ts vs constants.ts). The ACs require at least one tested override path.
data.title: Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing

## Summary
Add scene-level harness tests asserting real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames, framerate-independently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatScene` tests assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymWeapons` tests assert the same for the gym scene.
- [ ] **AC3** — Tests are framerate-independent (verify with different dt values).
- [ ] **AC4** — Tests cover multiple simultaneously active weapons phase-locked to the same grid.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC5** — [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.

## Key Files

# Unit Tests for Range-Based Positioning

**Goal:** As a developer, I want comprehensive unit tests for the new range-based positioning logic so that the behaviour is verified before implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **TAC1 — Test structure:** New test file `src/waves/WaveManager.spec.ts` (or equivalent) contains dedicated test cases for range-based positioning in `planGroupSpawns()`.
2. **TAC2 — min=max case:** Test verifies that when `startXMin === startXMax` and `startYMin === startYMax`, the base position equals those values exactly (deterministic).
3. **TAC3 — min<max case:** Test verifies that when ranges are active, the generated base position falls within `[startXMin, startXMax]` × `[startYMin, startYMax]`. Tests multiple random draws to confirm randomness within bounds.
4. **TAC4 — Reversed/invalid ranges:** Test verifies that reversed ranges (min > max) are handled gracefully (clamped or documented as error), with injected RNG.
5. **TAC5 — Integration with existing tests:** All existing unit and integration tests continue to pass alongside the new tests.
6. **TAC6 — No exact-position assertions:** Tests verify bounds and structural correctness, not exact positions, to accommodate randomness.

## Key Files
- `src/waves/WaveManager.spec.ts` — New or augmented test file for range positioning tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — Target file for `planGroupSpawns()` implementation

## Dependencies
- None (test-first; tests will initially fail until implementation)
data.title: AC7 — Unit tests for range-based positioning in planGroupSpawns

data.description:
# Add Range Fields to EnemyConfig

**Goal:** As a level designer, I want EnemyConfig to support configurable spawn-position ranges so that each wave can spawn enemies within a controlled band.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — EnemyConfig fields:** `EnemyConfig` gains `startXMin: number`, `startXMax: number`, `startYMin: number`, `startYMax: number` (all optional, defaulting to `undefined`).
2. **AC6a — Backward compat (scalar fallback):** When `startXMin` and `startXMax` are undefined (or equal), the effective start X equals `startX` (the existing scalar field). Same for Y. This preserves current behaviour exactly.
3. **AC6b — Default coercion:** Any code or store that reads these fields must coerce `undefined` to `startX`/`startY` respectively, so callers never need null checks.
4. **AC6c — No breaking changes:** Existing code that reads `EnemyConfig.startX` and `EnemyConfig.startY` continues to work unchanged.
5. **AC6d — Type safety:** TypeScript enforces that `startXMin ≤ startXMax` conceptually; runtime validation is handled at the config store / gym editor layer.

## Key Files
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — Add optional `startXMin`, `startXMax`, `startYMin`, `startYMax` to `EnemyConfig` interface

## Dependencies
- None (this is the foundational type change)
data.title: AC1+AC6 — Add startXMin/Max, startYMin/Max to EnemyConfig with backward compatibility

data.description:
# CSV Store Support for Range Fields

**Goal:** As a level designer, I want the CSV config store to read/write the four new range fields so that enemy spawn positions can be configured per enemy type.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC2a — CSV codec reads new fields:** `configStore.ts` parses `startXMin`, `startXMax`, `startYMin`, `startYMax` from CSV headers. Missing columns are treated as absent (defaulting to `undefined`).
2. **AC2b — CSV codec writes new fields:** When writing configs, the four new fields are included in CSV output.
3. **AC6c — Backward compatibility (CSV):** Existing CSV files without the new columns load successfully. Missing columns default to `undefined`, which the store coerces to the scalar `startX`/`startY` values.
4. **AC2c — configDefaults.ts updated:** Seed defaults in `configDefaults.ts` populate all four new fields with `min = max = current scalar value` for every enemy type.
5. **AC2d — No CSV file changes required:** The existing `enemy-configs.csv` does not need to be modified; the codec handles missing columns gracefully.

## Key Files
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — CSV codec: add parsing/writing for `startXMin`, `startXMax`, `startYMin`, `startYMax`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — Populate new fields (min = max) in all seed defaults

## Dependencies
- AH-0MUKI81200005YL4 (AC1+AC6 — EnemyConfig fields) — the type must exist before the store populates it
data.title: AC2+AC6 — CSV store support for new range fields

data.description:
# WaveGroup Range Fields

**Goal:** As a level designer, I want WaveGroup to also carry range fields so that per-wave overrides can be expressed if needed in the future, maintaining structural parity with EnemyConfig.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **WG1 — WaveGroup fields:** `WaveGroup` in `Formations.ts` gains optional `startXMin?`, `startXMax?`, `startYMin?`, `startYMax?` fields.
2. **WG2 — group() helper updated:** The `group()` shorthand helper accepts the four new optional parameters.
3. **WG3 — Backward compatibility:** Existing calls to `group()` without range parameters continue to work.
4. **WG4 — Priority:** When both WaveGroup and EnemyConfig specify ranges, WaveGroup takes precedence (per-level override).

## Key Files
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — Add range fields to WaveGroup interface and `group()` helper

## Dependencies
- AH-0MUKI81200005YL4 (AC1+AC6 — EnemyConfig fields) — same pattern, can proceed in parallel but type definitions should be consistent
data.title: AC4 — Add range fields to WaveGroup for consistency

Implementation notes (AC1–AC5). Files: src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts, src/utils/beat.ts, and tests in CombatCoreScene.test.ts / GymWeapons.test.ts / PlayScene.test.ts / beat.test.ts.

Changes:
- CombatCoreScene (the shared base for the game's CombatScene and the gym scenes) now owns a single BeatClock created once per scene and anchored at scene start (t=0): protected readonly beatClock (AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5).
- _autoFire injects that one instance into the player (player.setBeatClock) before tryFire, so player shots are phase-locked to the scene anchor and there is exactly one clock per scene — the game and every gym reuse the shared base, no per-scene duplicate (AC1/AC2/AC5).
- Added getBeatClock() accessor; added BeatClock.reset() so a scene restart can return the grid to its origin (used to make the scene audio tests deterministic).
- Pause behaviour is inherent: the clock advances only via _autoFire (from _tickPlayer, from update), so a paused scene pauses the clock (AC4).

Tests: added CombatCoreScene tests (single shared instance injected into the player; clock advances by dt*1000 and shots are exact grid ticks; separate scenes have separate instances) and GymWeapons tests (gym player shares the scene clock and fires on grid ticks; clock holds phase while paused). Build clean; full suite green (2505 tests, rebased onto 82a6be2d).
